subject: Cognitive Science
title: Source Confusion
description: A short lesson to help you apply Source Confusion.

hook.text: You know a fact but can't remember where you learned it. Was it a friend, a book, or a dream?

buildup.text: Source confusion is the failure to remember the origin of a memory while retaining its content.

discovery.text: The brain stores content and source separately. Content survives, but the source tag often fades first.

twist.text: This is how people plagiarize accidentally: a forgotten source makes someone else's idea feel like your own.

climax.text: Fake news exploits it. After a few days, you remember the claim but forget it came from a bad source.

punchline.text: You remember what, but forget where. That's the danger.

quiz.question: What is source confusion?
options: Remembering information but forgetting its origin
